canonical_goal: Deliver a governed declarative jurisdiction knowledge package lifecycle that compiles corpus-backed jurisdiction experts into the existing ExAIS runtime registry with fail-closed validation, operator promotion, reference migrations, and reproducible proof.

tickets.title: Define jurisdiction package schema
tickets.goal: Create the declarative contract for jurisdiction knowledge packages, covering package identity, versioning, corpus cards, acquisition, normalization and chunking, semantic representation, graphing, search, explanation, citation, evals, and named expert exposure.
tickets.acceptance: A package schema can express at least court decisions, statutes, municipal codes, administrative regulations, legislative materials, and meeting records, and validation reports missing required sections by corpus type.

tickets.title: Add version and evidence digest model
tickets.goal: Attach each package version to bounded, server-owned corpus evidence and deterministic digests so operators can prove which evidence produced a package.
tickets.acceptance: A package validation run emits package version, corpus evidence identifiers, source digests, generated artifact digests, and a stable package digest that changes when evidence or declarations change.

tickets.title: Implement package compiler
tickets.goal: Compile package declarations into the existing shared ExAIS expert registry and runtime-facing descriptors without creating a second registry or changing caller-facing expert IDs.
tickets.acceptance: Given a valid package with one or more experts, the compiler produces existing-registry-compatible expert entries and rejects output that would require a parallel runtime registry.

tickets.title: Enforce fail-closed governance boundaries
tickets.goal: Prevent generated or declarative package content from activating tenancy, RLS, scopes, citation authority, provider and security routing, memory authority, output guards, or tool ceilings.
tickets.acceptance: Validation fails closed when any package or generated draft attempts to set protected runtime controls, and tests show protected controls can only be referenced as externally managed constraints.

tickets.title: Model corpus-type extension contracts
tickets.goal: Add shared extension contracts for corpus connectors, metadata schemas, normalizers, chunkers, ontology selectors, caveats, search lenses, query planners, and eval families while allowing corpus-specific implementations.
tickets.acceptance: Each supported corpus type can declare its connector, metadata, chunking, graph, search, caveat, and eval strategy through typed extension points without custom compiler branches per jurisdiction.

tickets.title: Add graph and search descriptor contracts
tickets.goal: Represent corpus-specific graph ontologies, extractors, search lenses, specialized tools, and query-planning hints as package-owned declarations that the runtime can consume through existing search and graph paths.
tickets.acceptance: A package can declare both semantic search behavior and at least one specialized graph-backed search lens, and the compiled output exposes those descriptors to existing search/tool routing without bypassing governance.

tickets.title: Implement scaffold CLI
tickets.goal: Provide an operator command to scaffold a new jurisdiction package with manifest, corpus cards, expert declarations, eval stubs, and documentation placeholders.
tickets.acceptance: Running the scaffold command for a jurisdiction creates a package directory with valid placeholder files that pass structural validation while remaining inactive.

tickets.title: Build provider-agnostic drafting workflow
tickets.goal: Generate draft corpus cards, tool descriptions, expert instructions, and eval candidates from bounded server-owned store metadata, declared capabilities, and representative retrieval evidence.
tickets.acceptance: A generate command reads only bounded store metadata and representative retrieval evidence inputs, writes inactive draft package content with provenance, and never writes protected controls or activation state.

tickets.title: Add package diff and validation commands
tickets.goal: Give operators deterministic CLI feedback for generated versus promoted package content, schema errors, protected-control violations, digest changes, and registry compile results.
tickets.acceptance: The CLI can diff drafts against promoted packages and validate a package with machine-readable diagnostics, nonzero exit codes on failure, and no mutation during validation.

tickets.title: Add operator promotion lifecycle
tickets.goal: Implement explicit operator promotion, rollback, and deactivation for package versions while preserving fail-closed activation and auditable state transitions.
tickets.acceptance: Promote, rollback, and deactivate commands require an already-valid package digest, record lifecycle events, and never activate generated drafts without an explicit promotion command.

tickets.title: Implement package drift detection
tickets.goal: Detect drift between promoted package versions, corpus evidence digests, generated compiler outputs, and current server-owned store metadata.
tickets.acceptance: A drift command reports unchanged, changed, missing, and stale package evidence states with deterministic exit behavior suitable for scheduler or CI use.

tickets.title: Migrate Kansas Court Decisions package
tickets.goal: Express Kansas Court Decisions as a reference jurisdiction package using the new lifecycle while preserving existing caller IDs, retrieval behavior, citation support, and expert behavior.
tickets.acceptance: Kansas Court Decisions compiles through the package compiler into the existing expert registry with unchanged caller IDs and passing semantic search, graph, expert, session follow-up, and citation-support regression checks.

tickets.title: Migrate Topeka Municipal Code package
tickets.goal: Express Topeka Municipal Code as a reference jurisdiction package using municipal-code-specific corpus metadata, graph, search, caveats, evals, and expert declarations while preserving existing caller behavior.
tickets.acceptance: Topeka Municipal Code compiles through the package compiler with unchanged caller IDs and passing ordinance/code retrieval, specialized search, expert, follow-up, and citation-support regression checks.

tickets.title: Add deterministic compiler tests
tickets.goal: Cover schema validation, package digests, governance rejection, compiler registry output, lifecycle commands, and migration behavior with deterministic automated tests.
tickets.acceptance: A local test command proves valid packages compile, invalid protected controls fail closed, digests are stable, lifecycle transitions are explicit, and both reference migrations preserve expected IDs.

tickets.title: Add Docker and live behavior proof
tickets.goal: Provide reproducible Docker/live verification for semantic retrieval, specialized graph behavior, search tools, expert routing, session follow-up, and citation-support behavior for reference packages.
tickets.acceptance: Documented Docker/live commands exercise Kansas Court Decisions and Topeka Municipal Code packages end to end and capture proof for semantic, graph, tool, expert, follow-up, and citation-support behavior without relying on GitHub CI as the only gate.

tickets.title: Update setup and operator runbooks
tickets.goal: Document the complete package lifecycle for new ExAIS instances, including scaffold, generate, diff, validate, promote, rollback, deactivate, drift detection, proof collection, and protected-control boundaries.
tickets.acceptance: Setup and runbook documentation lets an operator create a new inactive jurisdiction package, draft it from bounded evidence, validate and promote it, roll it back or deactivate it, and run drift/proof commands without undocumented steps.
